clearedSpotChecks.check: Whether an ordinary account can reach compiled code on the networks.json endpoints through eth_call or switch it on.
clearedSpotChecks.note: web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-25 returned reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc for https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com and tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748 for https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz. reth_jit returned -32601 Method not found on Ethereum and -32601 method not allowed on Tempo. The evm2 runtime config at 66687c18 (crates/jit/runtime/src/runtime/config.rs) documents enabled as defaulting to false, jit_hot_threshold 8 and jit_max_bytecode_len 24 KiB with 0 meaning no limit, so compiled lookup is a node operator setting. The actor operator is correct for any JIT codegen fault.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Which PoolManager opcodes the JIT sends to builtins that wrap the interpreter's own arithmetic, and whether those builtins match the interpreter.
clearedSpotChecks.note: builtins/src/lib.rs lines 111-155 at 66687c18 were fetched. DIV and MOD return 0 for a zero divisor and otherwise call ruint wrapping_div and wrapping_rem; SDIV and SMOD call evm2 i256_div and i256_mod; ADDMOD and MULMOD call ruint add_mod and mul_mod with the third stack item as modulus; EXP charges exp_cost then calls pow. The rev! binding puts the top of stack first, which matches the specified operand order. The MULMOD with not(0) at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 therefore reaches the ruint mul_mod path, not a peephole rule, because 2^256-1 is not a power of two. The power of two rule in codegen/src/compiler/translate/peephole.rs (peephole_mulmod, peephole_addmod) masks the wrapping product or sum with m - 1, which is exact since 2^k divides 2^256, and moduli 0 and 1 fold to 0 as specified.

clearedSpotChecks.note: The cited op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 rust/Cargo.toml was fetched: lines 442-450 pin revm 43.x and a path dependency op-revm 20.0.0, and a search for evm2 or jit finds no entry.
